clue.text: Consequence of music downloaded illegally?

parts.note: a conviction leaves a lasting blot on one's file, while an illegally downloaded disc of music is itself a lawbreaking album

explanation.surface: A question about what happens to people who pirate songs online.
explanation.definitionFit: A conviction results in an official list of past offences, and pirated music is literally an unlawful disc.

clue.text: Labour politician without an injury

indicators.note: without here means losing, so the two letters of the following word are dropped from the politician's name

parts.note: Harriet Harman, a senior British Labour Party politician

explanation.surface: A Labour MP is left without a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: Harriet Harman was Labour's deputy leader when this appeared; take AN off her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm is damage or hurt done to someone, a near synonym of an injury.

clue.text: Bone of soft rock star

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
Elvis Presley, the king of rock and roll

explanation.surface: Asks which bone belonged to a gentle rock singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Elvis Presley was nicknamed 'Elvis the Pelvis' for his hip-swivelling, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelvis is the basin-shaped bone structure at the base of the spine.

clue.text: Just as cycle rider starts wobbling …

indicators.note: a wobbling bike rider unsettles the order, so these letters are shaken into a new arrangement
the start of the word rider supplies only its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cyclist barely manages as they set off unsteadily.
explanation.walkthrough: AS, CYCLE and R (start of 'rider') are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and barely both mean only by a narrow margin, as in 'just enough'.

clue.text: Fitting out a vessel in maritime industry

indicators.note: in places the vessel inside the industry word

parts.note: fishing is an industry carried on at sea
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: Describes equipping a ship for work at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Furnishing a room or ship means equipping it, fitting it out with what it needs.

clue.text: C minor composition is very short

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters of the key name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece written in C minor turns out to be brief.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a micron is a very short length rather than an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A micron is a millionth of a metre, an extremely small unit of length.

clue.text: Decoration for men with the last word in scripture

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: in puts the last word inside the scripture abbreviation

parts.note: NT is the New Testament
amen is the word that ends prayers and the Bible

explanation.surface: A medal awarded to soldiers with a closing word from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: AMEN is the final word of the New Testament, so the surface is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is an object worn or placed for decoration.

clue.text: Internet feature out west is a bit of a laugh

indicators.note: out means the letter for west is removed from the website name

parts.note: Twitter, the social media site

explanation.surface: A social media site popular out west is mildly amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: A titter is a short suppressed giggle, a small piece of laughter.

clue.text: Money to cover the Guardian is relative

indicators.note: the money word wraps round the other piece, covering it

parts.note: coin is money in metal pieces
the newspaper refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: Funding to support the newspaper comes from a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian speaking of itself is 'we' or 'us'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a family relation, a child of one's aunt or uncle.

clue.text: Setter is a Muslim leader

annotationWithheld.why: Setter is a Muslim leader (4): I'M + A + M, the M being the leader of 'Muslim', which also forms the definition 'Muslim leader'; one word doing two jobs, which the check refuses.

clue.text: Vary entire treatment for some non-NHS patients

indicators.note: a treatment works on the letters of both words, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Alter a whole course of care for those outside the health service.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS (Britain's National Health Service) treats people but not animals, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals are treated by vets rather than the NHS, so veterinary care serves them.

clue.text: Nude is condition without them

indicators.note: condition read as a verb means to work on or treat, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Being nude means having no knickers on.
explanation.walkthrough: An anagram of NUDE IS, with the whole clue also describing the answer; 'without them' completes the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being naked is the state of wearing no underwear, so the clue describes knickers by their absence.

clue.text: Play on a Dane quite unlikely to rise to the occasion

definitions.text: unlikely to rise to the occasion

indicators.note: playing on the words means toying with them, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hints at Hamlet, the indecisive Dane, failing in a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inadequate is not up to the task, unlikely to cope when tested.

clue.text: Plainchant used in service

parts.note: even means plain or level
a chant is a song

explanation.surface: Plainsong used during church worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plainchant' looks like one word for plainsong; split it as PLAIN + CHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening service of the Anglican church.

clue.text: Sign about worker to be shed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the sign goes round the worker

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A gesture about an employee who is to be discarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a verb ('to be shed'), but it is the noun, a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall.

clue.text: Youngster given support on horse by the Queen

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
a nag is an old horse
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A child is propped up on a horse beside the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Thousands carry about some Cadbury's Dairy Milk

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the carried letters read backwards
the chocolate bar's name carries the letters within it

explanation.surface: Lots of people carry some chocolate around.
explanation.walkthrough: Read DAIRY M backwards inside 'Dairy Milk'; Cadbury's is surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Myriad literally meant ten thousand, and now means countless.

clue.text: It's mad indeed to get name in paper

indicators.note: the deed is to receive the rest of the wordplay inside it

parts.note: read as in deed, a deed being a legal document

indicators.note: in places the name letter inside the paper

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper naming someone is said to be crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed' looks like an intensifier but splits as IN DEED, telling you where the rest goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Deranged describes someone insane, so 'it's mad' fits.

clue.text: Join inclination to space

indicators.note: to here means attached after, so the inclination follows the space

parts.note: an en is a printer's space
a list is a lean or inclination of a ship

explanation.surface: An instruction to add a tilt to a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to join the armed forces or a cause.

clue.text: Complimentary lead said to provide carte blanche

parts.note: complimentary means free of charge

indicators.note: said tells you the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: reign means to lead or rule

explanation.surface: A free dog lead supplied to give a pet full freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Free rein is complete liberty to act, the same idea as carte blanche.

clue.text: See 1
Sign from a dodgy guru, variable

indicators.note: dodgy means suspect or unsound, prompting a rearrangement

parts.note: Y is a mathematical variable

explanation.surface: An omen from a suspect spiritual teacher who varies.
explanation.definitionFit: An augury is an omen, a sign of what is to come.

clue.text: It's appropriate for girl to grab old flame

indicators.note: grab means to clutch, so the girl's name goes around the other piece

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: It is fitting for a girl to clutch a former lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To annexe territory is to seize or appropriate it.

clue.text: Calling for work?

definitions.meaning: work as a job or trade

explanation.walkthrough: A weak double definition; the two senses are close.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name a job: a calling is a vocation, and an occupation is the work one does for a living.

clue.text: Status of old film producer

definitions.meaning: standing or position in a hierarchy
J. Arthur ..., British film mogul whose films opened with a man striking a gong

explanation.definitionFit: Rank means status, and the Rank Organisation was a British film company.

clue.text: Way one's said to have gone by water

indicators.note: said shows the phrase is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: rowed means travelled by boat with oars

explanation.surface: A path someone is reported to have travelled by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a way or route between places.

clue.text: Do the twist — 21 without heroin

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the record word surrounds the drug

parts.note: the answer to 21, record, means write
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Dance the twist, a record free of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' seems to mean lacking, but here it means outside. 21 is RECORD, whose verb sense is WRITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm.

clue.text: Thanks for copper going from German port to Gibraltar, say

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the thanks letters replace the copper letters

parts.note: Cuxhaven, a port at the mouth of the Elbe
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: Gratitude for metal shipped from Germany to the Rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibraltar is an example of a low-tax territory used to shelter money.
